On October 19, 2026, Judge Ana C. Reyes held an evidentiary hearing in a contentious dispute concerning President Trump’s attempt  to replace a historic municipal golf course, accessible to people of all skillsets for a nominal fee, into a Trump-style championship course. She heard testimony from three witnesses: deputy chief of staff Gregory Wischer, of the Department of Interior; acting director of the National Parks Service Jessica Bowron; and Kevin Griess, NPS’s superintendent of National Mall and Memorial Parks. Senior Editors Roger Parloff and Molly Roberts live-blogged the hearing from the media room of the E. Barrett Prettyman U.S. Courthouse in Washington, D.C. You can read Parloff’s account by clicking on the liveblog button below or on Bluesky.Parloff Liveblog
At 10am Judge Ana Reyes will begin an evidentiary hearing in the golf course case at 10am. I'll try to live-blog from the US Courthouse media room for @lawfaremedia.org. This is a case to stop Trump from converting a historic public golf course, open to all, to a Trump style championship course. It's a fast-moving case. Last night Reyes denied a govt request to recuse herself. Trump said yesterday that he was closing the existing course Nov 15 (or earlier) to replace it. 2 days earlier govt attys called such plans were "conceptual," "nascent," & "preliminary."
